clue.text: Anglo-French bore.

parts.note: a bore is also a hole drilled through rock, here one dug jointly by Britain and France under the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: the rail link under the sea between Kent and Calais was drilled, or bored, by both countries.

clue.text: Warning relation about a line from Matilda, for example

indicators.note: about says the warning and the relation go round the other two pieces

parts.note: a caution is a warning
a relation is something related, a story or tale
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A relative gives a warning about a line spoken by a girl called Matilda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. Matilda, who told lies and was burned to death, is one of Hilaire Belloc's comic moral verses for children, published under this very title.
explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's poem Matilda is an example from his book of moral verses for children, each a story with a grim lesson.

clue.text: Theologian in drink is unsound

indicators.note: in places the theologian within the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar who has been drinking is not to be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes a rotten egg or a muddled brain, a synonym of faulty.

clue.text: A devoted fan of the Mirror, say?

definitions.text: A devoted fan of the Mirror, say?

parts.words: A devoted fan of the Mirror, say?
parts.note: not a loyal reader of the Daily Mirror newspaper but someone in love with a looking glass and the reflection in it

explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper, so the surface suggests a loyal reader; the capital letter hides an ordinary looking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of a self-admirer, named after the Greek youth who fell for his own reflection.

clue.text: Gifts distributed from huge liner

parts.note: huge means large
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, as in the name of a liner

explanation.surface: Presents are handed out from an enormous ocean ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or presents generously handed out, a synonym of bounty.

clue.text: European city with a slap-up buffet

indicators.note: to buffet is to knock about, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A continental town lays on a lavish self-service meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' reads as a spread of food but is the verb meaning to batter, which rearranges A SLAP UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swedish university town north of Stockholm, so an example of a place in Europe.

clue.text: Spoon on top of trunk

definitions.meaning: to spoon is an old word for kissing and cuddling
the part of the body directly above the torso

explanation.surface: A piece of cutlery lies on the lid of a travelling chest.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is slang for kissing and cuddling; as a noun it is the body part above the torso.

clue.text: Artist's model, not a clerical character

parts.note: lay describes someone who is not a member of the clergy
a figure is a character, a personage

explanation.surface: The person posing for a painter is certainly no churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A jointed wooden dummy that painters drape and pose in place of a live sitter.

clue.text: Game played by wasters — it's desirable to have bouncers

definitions.text: Game played by wasters — it's desirable to have bouncers

parts.words: Game played by wasters — it's desirable to have bouncers
parts.note: the pastime of skimming flat stones so they bounce across water, whose name is also an idiom for squandering money

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rowdy club needing doormen. To play this game with one's money is to squander it, and the game itself needs stones that bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimming stones across water goes by this name, and playing it with money is an idiom for squandering.

clue.text: Shore up masonry below screw

parts.note: below means under
a screw is a ship's or aircraft's propeller, prop for short

explanation.surface: A builder supports the stonework beneath a fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a wall or building from beneath, a synonym of underpin.

clue.text: Company back-up for fur producer

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for company

indicators.note: back sends the hyphenated word that follows it into the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A business provides support for a fur trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' splits: 'back' turns UP into PU. Company here is the army abbreviation COY, not the usual CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American rodent farmed for its pelt, sold as nutria.

clue.text: A tribe rebuffed in the City

parts.note: a means one, written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: rebuffed means turned back, so the two words after it are read from the far end

parts.note: taken as written
EC is the postcode district of the City of London, the financial quarter

explanation.surface: A clan gets the cold shoulder from London's financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' looks like a snub but turns the following words round, giving CENI. The City is London's financial district, whose postcode crosswords borrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca's ancient British people of East Anglia are an example.

clue.text: Eastern proverb said he was the first Edomite

indicators.note: said tells us the proverb is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: An oriental saying names the founder of the people of Edom.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob's brother in Genesis was also called Edom, and his descendants became that nation.

clue.text: Flower is the acme of perfection

definitions.meaning: a garden plant of the dianthus family, related to the carnation
the peak of condition or excellence, as in an idiom about being in very good health

explanation.surface: A blossom is as flawless as anything can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A dianthus bloom, and also the peak of condition as in the idiom about good health.

clue.text: Timid person frightened by unknown animal

parts.note: frightened means scared
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A nervous soul is alarmed by a mysterious beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish taunt for a coward, a synonym of chicken.

clue.text: Vocally, knight's daughter seems in distress

definitions.note: spoken, knight's is night's: the goddess meant was the child of Nyx, the Greek personification of night

indicators.note: letters in distress are disturbed, so the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: From her voice, the nobleman's girl sounds upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' rearranges SEEMS IN. The definition is itself a pun: said out loud, knight is night, and the Greek goddess of retribution was the daughter of Nyx, Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of retribution was the child of Nyx, Night, which is what knight's becomes when spoken.

clue.text: False confidence in motorway leading to second conviction

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, its figure 1 written as the letter I
a conviction is a firmly held belief

explanation.surface: Overconfidence on the fast road earns a driver another court judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistaken or wrongly held opinion, trust placed in something untrue.

clue.text: A new variety, for such a blue flower

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the two words after 'for' are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a fresh cultivar of a blue bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks back at nothing but governs 'such a', giving CHUSA after A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant of the borage family with vivid azure blooms, also called alkanet.

clue.text: Defies forbears

definitions.meaning: stands up to or opposes someone
holds back from doing something tempting, as a verb rather than the noun for ancestors

explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs are synonyms: to oppose or withstand, and to hold back from something tempting.

clue.text: Taking the mickey out of racist, I get roughed up

indicators.note: being roughed up is being knocked about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After mocking a bigot, the speaker is beaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the mickey is British slang for mocking, and the adjective describes mocking humour.

clue.text: Warn to fall back, being without clear round

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece sits outside the second
back turns the word for fall the other way

parts.note: to fall is to drop

indicators.note: round turns the word for clear about

parts.note: to clear a sum is to net it as profit

explanation.surface: Troops are told to retreat after failing to get through a stage unscathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives PORD and 'round' gives TEN; 'being without' means being outside. On the surface a clear round is a faultless showjumping circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or give an omen of trouble, a synonym of presage.

clue.text: Key player in a club perhaps

definitions.text: Key player in a club perhaps

parts.words: Key player in a club perhaps
parts.note: not a star footballer but a musician at the keyboard, who might perform in a nightclub

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of a musician whose instrument has keys and who may entertain in a nightclub.

clue.text: About to: encounter swarm

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for encounter faces the other way

parts.note: to encounter is to meet

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of running into a cloud of bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns MEET round. The phrase 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', which hides the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to be crowded or abound with moving things.

clue.text: Way round a colonnade

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A path circles a row of columns.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered walk lined with columns in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Kind of art right for scenery

parts.note: Art Deco is a decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s

explanation.surface: A certain style of painting suits the backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre, the stage setting or backdrop.

clue.text: Faith in firm in debt? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in signals one piece inside the other
the phrase swaps the roles, so the debt goes inside the firm rather than the firm inside the debt

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the red is debt, as in a bank account in the red

explanation.surface: Would anyone trust a business that owes money? Not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' reverses what 'in' says: not firm in debt but debt (RED) in firm (CO).
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of religious belief, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Matinée favourite left after one act

indicators.note: after places the letter for left behind the other two pieces

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to act is to do

explanation.surface: The darling of the afternoon audience walked out when the first act ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinée one is a handsome actor adored by afternoon audiences.

clue.text: The proprietor, a fat individual, is inside

indicators.note: is inside says the individual sits within the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
an individual is one, written I

explanation.surface: The owner, a portly man, is indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish landowner, the owner of an estate.

clue.text: Ticket for future use by artist under threat

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
a chess king under threat of capture is in check

explanation.surface: A painter in danger holds on to a pass for a later date.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a stub letting a spectator return another day when weather stops play.

clue.text: Loose file with quotations embodying happy expressions

indicators.note: loose letters are not fixed in place, so the word after it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
citations are quotations from a source

explanation.surface: An unbound folder of famous sayings contains some cheerful phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal congratulations, good wishes offered on a joyful occasion.
